title: Coordinated Shipwave Orchestrator: Shift-Choreography & Cross-Team Duty Roster
creator: Sana Kapoor
description: Introduce a lightweight Shipwave Orchestrator and operational pattern called 'shift-choreography' to coordinate rolling shipwaves across runtime, console, and API surfaces. This initiative formalizes a short-duty roster (4–6 week rotation) for launch weeks so that ownership, mitigation playbooks, and escalation paths are explicit across teams. The orchestrator is not a new service — it is a calendar-as-code + guardrail pattern plus a small orchestration dashboard that synthesizes capacity signals, scheduled shipwaves, and firewalled rollback triggers. Goal: reduce cross-team conflicts, remove ambiguous oncall handoffs during launches, and shorten time-to-safe-rollback when regressions surface.
goals: Formalize shipwave windows and dependency lanes for runtime, console, API with automated collision detection
Define a 6-person duty roster pattern and rotation cadence; provide runbook templates for each role
Automate pre-flight checks (capacity, model-compat, SLO health) to gate each shipwave step
Reduce launch-related incident MTTR by 30% and avoid simultaneous capacity pressure across surfaces

success_metrics: >= 90% of pre-flight checks green before canary step
Duty roster adoption across runtime/console/api teams >= 80%
acceptance_criteria: Calendar-as-code config can auto-detect overlapping shipwaves and block create with clear reasoning
Duty roster template checked into docs with role responsibilities and escalation contact list
Pre-flight automation runs and reports pass in staging for 3 consecutive runs
Dashboard displays active shipwaves, owners, capacity corridors and rollback markers
Post-shipwave retrospective template collected and actionable items tracked
risks: Teams skip the duty roster during busy weeks leading to ambiguous ownership
Pre-flight checks produce false positives and block legitimate launches
Orchestrator introduces extra process friction and delays small hotfixes
Calendar integration fails to surface late dependencies (third-party schedulers)
mitigations: Make duty roster minimal — 1 week handoffs preferred for small launches; opt-out only via exec sign-off
Tune pre-flight thresholds and provide an override path with audit logging
Allow 'fast-track' carve-outs for critical hotfixes with two-person approval
Add a lightweight dependency registration step in PR templates so teams declare cross-surface impacts early
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal pilot with runtime infra and console teams for 4 shipwaves
Phase 2: Expand to API surface and include dedicated customers lanes
Phase 3: Integrate with Dedicated customer calendar and provide tenant-level guardrails
Fallback: revert to pre-orchestrator release schedule for any shipwave failing 2 consecutive gates
communication_plan: Weekly launch sync (30m) during pilot with rotating facilitator from duty roster
#shipwave-orchestrator Slack channel for real-time signals and coordination
Automated daily digest email with next 7 days of scheduled shipwaves and owners
Post-shipwave retrospective published to Confluence and linked in the ticket
